note: Literal bytes; nothing here depends on the daemon's real port. Host port 65535 is fake and matches the default allowed-hosts wildcard 127.0.0.1:*. The token is a corpus fixture (fixed) so the case stream is byte-reproducible; it is delivered via MCP_NODE_TOKEN_FILE like ci/test_regressions.py does.

cases.description: Canonical valid ping: strict grammar, every gate passes. Baseline for mutations (base_case) and proof the harness talks to a healthy daemon.
cases.send:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 40

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
cases.notes: RFC 9112-clean request; connection stays keep-alive. Probe: with a half-closed client the server answers, then sees clean EOF in its keep-alive loop and closes; the answer itself still proves the connection stayed usable for that request.

cases.description: Duplicate Content-Length with identical values (class a). Accepted: RFC 9112 6.3 permits collapsing identical duplicates.
cases.send:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 40
Content-Length: 40

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
cases.notes: parseHead compares duplicates: equal values are collapsed, unequal are rejected. Probe: with a half-closed client the server answers, then sees clean EOF in its keep-alive loop and closes; the answer itself still proves the connection stayed usable for that request.

cases.description: Duplicate Content-Length with conflicting values (class b): classic request-smuggling split. Must be 400, never a guess or last-wins.
cases.send:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 40
Content-Length: 39

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
cases.notes: RFC 9112 6.3: conflicting duplicates ought to be treated as an error; smuggling-resistant answer is 400 + close.

cases.description: Content-Length + Transfer-Encoding: chunked (class c): the canonical CL.TE smuggling vector.
cases.send:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 40
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
cases.notes: RFC 9112 6.1: both present ought to be an error; the server refuses Transfer-Encoding outright (400).

cases.description: Content-Length + Transfer-Encoding: identity (class d): legacy-coding variant of the CL.TE desync.
cases.send:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 40
Transfer-Encoding: identity

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
cases.notes: RFC 9112 6.1: chunked is not the final encoding -> server MUST answer 400. Blanket TE refusal also matches.

cases.description: Transfer-Encoding: chunked without Content-Length. Framing would fall to chunked parsing; the server refuses any TE.
cases.send:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Transfer-Encoding: chunked

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
cases.notes: Stricter than RFC needs (a non-chunked-speaker MAY 501); refusing TE outright is the documented hardening stance.

cases.description: Bare LF as line terminator (class e), client half-closes after send: no CRLFCRLF ever appears, so the head never terminates; EOF mid-head must answer 400, not a hang.
cases.send:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 40

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
cases.notes: RFC 9112 2.2: a recipient MAY accept bare LF; strict CRLF-only is the safe desync-resistant posture.

cases.description: Bare LF head, client keeps the connection open: the head never completes, so the absolute request deadline (MCP_NODE_SOCKET_TIMEOUT_S=3) must fire a 408 in bounded time, never an open-ended hang.
cases.send:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 40

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
cases.notes: 408 must arrive near the 3s budget, not a fresh per-read timeout stacked on it.

cases.description: Bare CR as line terminator (class f), client half-closes: no LF at all, head never terminates, EOF mid-head -> 400.
cases.send: POST /mcp HTTP/1.1Host: 127.0.0.1:65535Content-Type: application/jsonX-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323Content-Length: 40{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
cases.notes: CR-only framing is invalid; the head scan only terminates on CRLFCRLF.

cases.description: Valid CRLF head, but a bare CR smuggled inside a header value (X-Junk: a<CR>b): field-content forbids CR, so header grammar must reject.
cases.send:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
X-Junk: ab
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 40

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}
cases.notes: RFC 9110 field-content: SP/HTAB/VCHAR/obs-text only; 0x0d is a grammar violation.

cases.description: Head complete, body truncated to 30 of the declared 40 bytes, then client half-closes (class g): short body must be 400 ShortBody, not a silent drop.
cases.send:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 40

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"metho
cases.notes: EOF mid-body: the declared body never fully arrived -> 400 ShortBody + close.

cases.description: Content-Length 1024 but only 10 body bytes, then client half-closes (class h): immediate EOF mid-body -> 400 ShortBody, never a hang.
cases.send:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 1024

{"jsonrpc
cases.notes: 104,182 bytes of the declared body never arrive; EOF shortens the wait to zero.

cases.description: Content-Length 1024, 10 bytes sent, client holds the connection open (class h): the server must give up at its absolute deadline (~3s) with 408, not hang.
cases.send:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 1024

{"jsonrpc
cases.notes: Absolute request deadline covers head+body; a dribbling client cannot pin a slot forever.

cases.description: Pipelining: two full valid requests written in one shot (class i): both answered in order, ids 1 then 2, no desync.
cases.send:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 40

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 40

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"ping"}
cases.notes: Over-fetched bytes past request 1 seed the next iteration (carry); answers stay in order. Probe: with a half-closed client the server answers, then sees clean EOF in its keep-alive loop and closes; the answer itself still proves the connection stayed usable for that request.

cases.description: Pipelining: valid request + second request with conflicting duplicate Content-Length (class j): first answered 200, the smuggled second must be 400 and the connection closed.
cases.send:
POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 40

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"ping"}POST /mcp HTTP/1.1
Host: 127.0.0.1:65535
Content-Type: application/json
X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 40
Content-Length: 1

{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":2,"method":"ping"}
cases.notes: The pipelined malformed head arrives via carry; parseHead rejects, connection closes: no desync window.

cases.description: Pipelining: valid request + second request whose declared Content-Length (10) exceeds the 3 bytes actually sent (class j variant): first 200, second 400 ShortBody.
cases.send:

X-Node-Token: fuzzcafe20261002c70c323
Content-Length: 10

abc
cases.notes: Truncation arriving as a pipelined second request: EOF mid-body -> 400 + close.

cases.description: Connect and half-close with zero bytes: clean EOF before any byte is the keep-alive shutdown path; the server must close silently, never emit a zombie 400.
cases.notes: Closed-without-response class: writing an error into a dying socket would be noise, not safety.

cases.description: Pipelining: valid request + second request with bare-LF framing: the carry path must treat the unterminated second head as BadHeaders on EOF, answering 200 then 400.
